question: Is personal data (PII) automatically redacted from prompts before they are transmitted to any third-party LLM provider?

Which categories of personal and financial identifiers (email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, payment card numbers, national identifiers such as PPSN/SSN) are detected, and is detection coverage regularly tested?
Do your audit logs apply data minimisation, i.e. are raw prompts and customer personal data excluded from stored log records?
Does the system automatically record events (logs) for every AI interaction over its lifetime, as required for record-keeping?
Can each logged AI interaction be traced to the exact policy version and configuration that was in force at the time?
What technical controls defend against prompt injection and attempts to manipulate the model into ignoring its instructions or exfiltrating data?
Are blocked or policy-violating requests recorded with a timestamp and reason so that ICT-related incidents can be detected, classified and reported?
Can we, our auditors or a competent authority independently verify the completeness of your audit trail without relying on vendor attestations (audit rights over ICT third-party providers)?
Are there enforced usage limits (token and cost ceilings) with an automatic circuit breaker to prevent runaway consumption or denial-of-wallet?
Is every outbound call to a third-party model provider logged with the provider and model used, supporting our register of information on ICT third-party arrangements?
Are audit logs cryptographically protected against tampering (e.g. hash-chaining), and how is integrity proven?
How do you detect and remediate application code that calls LLM provider APIs directly, bypassing the security gateway (shadow AI)?
